vocabulary.meaning_en: a comfortable, natural way of doing something well
vocabulary.note_ar: تأتي أيضاً في in the groove أي يعمل بانسجام وسهولة.
vocabulary.note_en: Also 'in the groove' = working well and easily.
vocabulary.example: After a month, she found her groove at the new school.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a period of time with a special character
vocabulary.example: We are living in the digital era.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a toothed wheel in a machine or car
vocabulary.example: Change into second gear when you go up the hill.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to rub hard or crush into small pieces
to make someone a little angry
vocabulary.example: Loud phones on the bus annoy me.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small cupboard with a lock, e.g. at school or a gym
vocabulary.example: I left my bag in my locker.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the part of a bird used for flying
to keep someone safe from harm
a person who has just arrived or joined
vocabulary.example: The team welcomed the newcomer warmly.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to know someone or something because you saw it before
vocabulary.example: I didn't recognise you with glasses!

vocabulary.meaning_en: to know exactly what something is
vocabulary.example: Something is different, but I can't put my finger on it.
He refused to change his answer.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the journey to and from work every day
vocabulary.note_ar: تأتي فعلاً أيضاً: I commute by train.
vocabulary.note_en: Also a verb: I commute by train.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an activity you enjoy in your free time
to say that you are not happy about something

vocabulary.example: There is a strange smell in the kitchen.

fine_lines.title: Find your groove vs be in my ... era
fine_lines.explanation_ar: find your groove تعني أن تصبح مرتاحاً وماهراً في شيء بعد بداية صعبة. أما in my ... era فتعني أنك تركّز على اهتمام معيّن في هذه الفترة من حياتك.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Find your groove' = become comfortable and good at something after a hard start. 'In my ... era' = a period of your life when you focus on one interest.

examples.sentence: The new job was hard at first, but I've found my groove.
I'm in my reading era - I finish a book every week.

fine_lines.title: A you problem vs grinds my gears
fine_lines.explanation_ar: a you problem تقولها لتوضّح أن المشكلة تخص الشخص الآخر وليست مسؤوليتك. أما grinds my gears فتعني أن شيئاً يزعجك أنت كثيراً.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'A you problem' says the problem belongs to the other person, not you. 'It grinds my gears' says something really annoys you.

examples.sentence: You forgot your umbrella? That's a you problem.
People who push in the queue really grind my gears.

expressions.meaning_en: to become comfortable and confident doing something
expressions.example: It took me a few weeks, but I've found my groove in the new office.

expressions.meaning_en: in a period of your life when you focus on one activity or interest
expressions.example: I've visited five cities this year - I'm in my travel era.
It really grinds my gears when people don't reply to emails.

expressions.meaning_ar: عندك شيء إضافي جاهز (مهارة أو فكرة)
expressions.meaning_en: to have an extra skill or idea ready to use
expressions.example: Don't worry about dinner - I've got a few good recipes in my locker.

expressions.meaning_en: to help, guide and protect someone, often someone new
expressions.example: When I joined the company, Sara took me under her wing.

expressions.meaning_en: an informal way to say the problem is yours, not mine
expressions.example: You stayed up until 2 a.m.? That sounds like a you problem.

expressions.meaning_en: however much you do it, it won't change the situation
expressions.example: You can ask all you like, but the shop is closed.

expressions.phrase: can't put my finger on it
expressions.meaning_en: I can't say exactly what it is
expressions.example: Something about this room is different, but I can't put my finger on it.

grammar.title: Possessive adjectives in fixed expressions
grammar.explanation_ar: في هذه التعابير تتغيّر كلمة الملكية حسب الشخص: my / your / his / her / our / their. نقول: I found my groove, She found her groove, They found their groove. والتعبير a you problem استثناء طريف: نضع الضمير you قبل الاسم كأنه صفة.
grammar.explanation_en: In these expressions the possessive word changes with the person: my / your / his / her / our / their. 'A you problem' is a fun exception: 'you' is used before the noun like an adjective.
examples: She took him under her wing.
They have a few tricks in their locker.
That's a you problem, not a me problem.

questions.question: What does 'it grinds my gears' mean?
questions.explanation_ar: grind my gears تعني أن الشيء يزعجني كثيراً.
questions.explanation_en: It means something annoys you a lot.

questions.question: After a hard start in her new job, Mona has finally ___ .
questions.explanation_ar: find your groove = تعتاد وتصبح ماهراً بعد بداية صعبة.
questions.explanation_en: 'Find your groove' = become comfortable and good at something.

questions.question: 'I'm in my baking era' means:
choices: I baked a long time ago
These days I focus on baking
questions.explanation_ar: in my ... era = في هذه الفترة أركّز على هذا النشاط.
questions.explanation_en: It means baking is your main interest at this time.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: She took him under her wing.
She took him under his wing.
She took him under the wings.
She took him on her wing.
questions.explanation_ar: الصيغة الصحيحة take someone under your wing، والملكية تعود على من يقدّم المساعدة (her).
questions.explanation_en: The possessive refers to the helper: 'she ... her wing'.

questions.question: 'You can shout all you like' means:
questions.explanation_ar: all you like = مهما فعلت لن يتغير الوضع.
questions.explanation_en: However much you shout, the situation won't change.

questions.question: I know this song, but I can't ___ on where I heard it.
questions.explanation_ar: can't put my finger on it = لا أستطيع تحديده بدقة.
questions.explanation_en: 'Can't put my finger on it' = can't say exactly what it is.

questions.question: Which expression means 'an extra skill you have ready to use'?
questions.explanation_ar: have something in your locker = لديك مهارة أو فكرة إضافية جاهزة.
questions.explanation_en: 'Have something in your locker' = have something extra ready.

questions.question: A friend complains he is tired because he played games all night. A cheeky reply is:
questions.explanation_ar: a you problem = هذه مشكلتك أنت.
questions.explanation_en: 'That's a you problem' = it's your problem, not mine.

questions.question: Which one is about ANNOYANCE, not about getting comfortable?
questions.explanation_ar: grind your gears عن الإزعاج، أما find your groove فعن الاعتياد والإتقان.
questions.explanation_en: 'Grind your gears' is about annoyance; the others are not.

questions.question: Choose the best word: 'Our teacher ___ the new student under her wing.'
questions.explanation_ar: الفعل الصحيح مع هذا التعبير هو take (الماضي took).
questions.explanation_en: The verb in this expression is 'take' (past: took).
